title: Funding a Wallet and Running a Live Testnet Trade
text: Hyperliquid’s deposit screen asks “USDC Arbitrum,” newcomers (including us) get stuck. vocabulary: USDC stablecoin – digital US dollar, worth ~$1. money Hyperliquid account trades . Arbitrum company, platform, account – nothing sign KYC. network: think cheaper express lane built top Ethereum. Hyperliquid accepts USDC sitting Arbitrum lane. HYPE Hyperliquid’s token (staking, fees, governance, trading). cash account trades , holding HYPE fund account. Snag hit #1 – “thought Ethereum just Ethereum.” now one main Ethereum network plus several cheaper “layer-2” lanes built (Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, …). coin can live different lanes, coin one lane used another bridged across. Snag #2 – fees paid ETH, USDC. Every move network costs fee (“gas”), lane charges gas ETH. USDC started main Ethereum lane, first needed little ETH Ethereum move – later little ETH Arbitrum deposit. Moving $9 ended needing ~$1 ETH gas, swap ETH onto Arbitrum. Snag #3 – main Ethereum lane expensive. Moving small amounts Ethereum mainnet can cost several dollars gas. Cheaper ways land USDC little ETH directly Arbitrum (skipping costly hops): centralised exchange withdrawal, choosing Arbitrum network (flat fee, slippage) – needs KYC account. dedicated bridge Across Jumper (tighter pricing wallet’s built-bridge). wallets support Arbitrum directly can send MetaMask Arbitrum. switch USDC Ethereum Arbitrum used MetaMask’s built-Bridge (“swap”): USDC Ethereum USDC Arbitrum. Snag #4 – MetaMask’s swap/bridge takes cut. charges service fee (~0.9%) plus slippage. Convenient, cheapest route (see bridges ).

Leverage lets small amount collateral control larger position (e.g. 5x). magnifies gains losses, can trigger liquidation (position force-closed) adverse move. text: One typed method, one data.table, list columns — lossless escape hatch. Every typed method returns flat data.table; nested API objects flattened scalar columns, heterogeneous rows stacked discriminator column (side, delta_type, status, …). byte-faithful archive needs venue’s records instead tidy table, *_raw() sibling (e.g. get_funding_history_raw()) returns Hyperliquid’s parsed JSON untouched — decimal strings, field order, null-vs-absent preserved. Sync async. Every method works modes. async = TRUE returns promise; otherwise results returned directly. single sync/async branch point (connectcore::then_or_now(), hyperliquid_build_request() delegates ). Shared transport base via github.com/dereckscompany/connectcore. API camelCase fields become snake_case columns; prices sizes returned numerics. Pure-R Ethereum signing via github.com/dereckscompany/ethsign. secp256k1 ECDSA, Keccak-256, EIP-712 come standalone pure-R ethsign package; Hyperliquid-specific msgpack action hash lives . compiled code, verified byte-identical test vectors official Hyperliquid Python SDK (v0.24.0), used reference implementation. One host, two paths. whole REST API lives behind one host: /info (public reads) /exchange (signed writes). network chosen explicit testnet flag, never URL sniffing, network changes signature .
